claims.statement: UNESCO places the northern Japanese sequence represented by these sites at approximately 13,000–400 BCE.

value.text: UNESCO places the northern Japanese sequence represented by these sites at approximately 13,000–400 BCE.

claims.statement: Settled communities relied on hunting, fishing and gathering; their sites preserve dwellings, graves, earthworks and stone circles.

value.text: Settled communities relied on hunting, fishing and gathering; their sites preserve dwellings, graves, earthworks and stone circles.

claims.statement: The official site guide dates the settlement at Sannai Maruyama to approximately 3900–2200 BCE.

value.text: The official site guide dates the settlement at Sannai Maruyama to approximately 3900–2200 BCE.

claims.statement: At Aomori, planned dwellings, storage pits and roads accompanied a diet evidenced by nuts, fish and animal remains; imported materials included jade and obsidian.

value.text: At Aomori, planned dwellings, storage pits and roads accompanied a diet evidenced by nuts, fish and animal remains; imported materials included jade and obsidian.

claims.statement: UNESCO dates the dolmen tombs at Gochang, Hwasun and Ganghwa broadly to the first millennium BCE.

value.text: UNESCO dates the dolmen tombs at Gochang, Hwasun and Ganghwa broadly to the first millennium BCE.

claims.statement: These cemeteries preserve hundreds of tombs assembled from large stone slabs.

value.text: These cemeteries preserve hundreds of tombs assembled from large stone slabs.

claims.statement: The Dilmun burial mounds in western Bahrain were built approximately 2200–1750 BCE.

value.text: The Dilmun burial mounds in western Bahrain were built approximately 2200–1750 BCE.

claims.statement: Bahrain’s role as a trading centre supported elaborate burial traditions, preserved in extensive mound fields and royal tombs.

value.text: Bahrain’s role as a trading centre supported elaborate burial traditions, preserved in extensive mound fields and royal tombs.

claims.statement: The Met’s chronology places Lapita settlement of Island Melanesia and western Polynesia around 1500–500 BCE.

value.text: The Met’s chronology places Lapita settlement of Island Melanesia and western Polynesia around 1500–500 BCE.

claims.statement: Communities expanded eastward across the western Pacific and made distinctively decorated pottery.

value.text: Communities expanded eastward across the western Pacific and made distinctively decorated pottery.

claims.statement: The Met dates the emergence of Arnhem Land’s X-ray rock-art style to around 2000 BCE and describes it as continuing to the present.

value.text: The Met dates the emergence of Arnhem Land’s X-ray rock-art style to around 2000 BCE and describes it as continuing to the present.

claims.statement: Artists depicted internal organs and bones within human and animal figures.

value.text: Artists depicted internal organs and bones within human and animal figures.

claims.statement: UNESCO dates the Chavín cultural context in this Peruvian highland valley to approximately 1500–300 BCE.

value.text: UNESCO dates the Chavín cultural context in this Peruvian highland valley to approximately 1500–300 BCE.

claims.statement: Its place of worship includes terraces, plazas and dressed-stone structures with animal-like ornament.

value.text: Its place of worship includes terraces, plazas and dressed-stone structures with animal-like ornament.

claims.statement: The map uses UNESCO’s reference position for Chavín’s ceremonial landscape, not a territorial boundary.
The National Park Service dates residential and ceremonial use of Poverty Point to approximately 1700–1100 BCE.

value.text: The National Park Service dates residential and ceremonial use of Poverty Point to approximately 1700–1100 BCE.

claims.statement: Hunter-fisher-gatherers built monumental earthworks in the Lower Mississippi Valley and participated in far-reaching exchange networks.

value.text: Hunter-fisher-gatherers built monumental earthworks in the Lower Mississippi Valley and participated in far-reaching exchange networks.

claims.statement: The map uses UNESCO’s reference position for Poverty Point’s mound builders, not a territorial boundary.
UNESCO places Sammallahdenmäki in the Scandinavian Bronze Age context of approximately 1500–500 BCE.

value.text: UNESCO places Sammallahdenmäki in the Scandinavian Bronze Age context of approximately 1500–500 BCE.

claims.statement: Communities built granite burial cairns in clusters along a ridge in western Finland.

value.text: Communities built granite burial cairns in clusters along a ridge in western Finland.

claims.statement: The map uses UNESCO’s reference position for Sammallahdenmäki’s burial cairns, not a territorial boundary.
UNESCO describes the monumental city’s building period broadly as the first through seventh centuries CE.

value.text: UNESCO describes the monumental city’s building period broadly as the first through seventh centuries CE.

claims.statement: Large pyramids and temples formed part of a city laid out according to geometric and symbolic principles.
